headline: Impossible Filter Gallery Transition achieved with CSS Only, no JavaScript required
summary: A developer showcases a filterable image gallery that achieves complex transitions using only CSS, defying expectations of JavaScript. The technique relies on custom variables for dynamic positioning.
details: A new experiment demonstrates an "impossible" filter gallery transition built entirely with CSS, challenging the common assumption that such interactivity requires JavaScript. The technique allows users to filter and rearrange images with smooth animations.

The core of the solution lies in the clever use of CSS custom variables. These variables, such as --l, --t, --x, and --y, are used to control the default and clicked positions of cards, enabling dynamic layout changes.

The developer utilized a "hardcoded-variable trick" discovered in 2024 to manage card placements. While effective, this method currently requires some hardcoding due to CSS limitations, prompting plans for a simpler, less hardcoded future version.

Responsiveness is also handled through custom variables, with separate sets like --l1, --t1, --x1, and --y1 for different breakpoints. This allows the gallery to adapt its layout across various screen sizes.

The project includes a lightbox feature and suggests adding more custom variables for additional breakpoints, similar to frameworks like Bootstrap. The creator plans to release a video and tutorial soon for a less hardcoded approach.
